reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space, equipped with a measurable structure whose measurable sets are the Borel sets. Let V:E->R and let kappa be a nonnegative real number. Assume kappa>=1, V is twice continuously Frechet differentiable, and, for every x,v in E, (1/kappa)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2. Let eta,c,eps be real numbers satisfying 0<eta<=c<1 and eps>0. Let nu be a probability measure on E such that y |-> ||grad V(y)||^2 is integrable. For y in E define T_y:E->E by T_y(x)=y-eta grad V(x), and define C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c). Then there exist measurable functions p:E->E and N:E->N such that y |-> T_y^[N(y)](y) is measurable and, for every y in E, p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y, ||T_y^[N(y)](y)-p(y)||<=eps, and Q(grad V,eta,eps,y,N(y)+1,y)=some((T_y^[N(y)](y),N(y)+1)). Moreover, y |-> N(y)+1 is integrable with respect to nu and integral (N(y)+1) dnu(y) <= C(1+log(1+sqrt(integral ||grad V(y)||^2 dnu(y))/eps)). Here T_y^[n] denotes n-fold iteration (with the zeroth iterate equal to the identity), and Q is the stated exact-real recursive interpreter, so N(y)+1 is the number of gradient-oracle evaluations, including the successful test.
objects: The ambient space E; the potential V and its gradient and Hessian; the condition number parameter kappa; the step size eta, contraction-control parameter c, and accuracy eps; the probability measure nu; the parameterized fixed-point map T_y(x)=y-eta grad V(x); the constant C; the interpreter Q; and the existential measurable witness functions p and N.
domains: E is a finite-dimensional complete normed real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. V maps E to R. kappa lies in the nonnegative reals and is coerced to R in the Hessian bound. eta,c,eps and C are real. nu is a probability measure on E. T_y and p map E to E, N maps E to the natural numbers, and Q returns an optional pair in E x N.
quantifiers: Universally quantified are E with all displayed algebraic, topological, finite-dimensional, and measurable structures; V; kappa; eta,c,eps; and the probability measure nu. The Hessian inequalities are universal in x,v in E. After these data and assumptions, there exist functions p:E->E and N:E->N. Their fixed-point, approximation, and Q-return properties hold for every y in E.
assumptions: kappa>=1. V is C^2. For every x,v, the Hessian quadratic form satisfies (1/kappa)||v||^2 <= D^2V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2. The scalars satisfy 0<eta<=c<1 and eps>0. nu has total mass one, and ||grad V||^2 is nu-integrable.
conclusion: There are measurable p and N, with the selected N-th iterate measurable, such that p(y) solves the proximal equation p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y; the iterate T_y^[N(y)](y) is within eps of p(y); and Q, started at y with fuel N(y)+1, returns that iterate together with the exact evaluation count N(y)+1. This count is integrable and its expectation is at most C times 1+log(1+sqrt(E_nu[||grad V||^2])/eps).
scopes: T_y is defined after eta and by holding y fixed while iterating in x. C is defined from c alone. Both local definitions are in scope for the existential witnesses and all following assertions. The witnesses p and N may depend on every preceding universally quantified datum and assumption. The pointwise properties are inside the scope of 'for every y'; the integrability and expectation bound are global statements under nu.
constant_dependencies: C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c) depends only on c. The bound also depends explicitly on eps and on nu and V through sqrt(integral ||grad V||^2 dnu). T_y depends on y, eta, and V. The existential p and N may additionally depend on E, kappa, c, eps, nu, and all preceding structure and hypotheses, although p's defining proximal equation itself uses only y, eta, and V. No dimension factor or additional dependence on kappa appears explicitly in the displayed expectation bound.
